tasks.title: Autonomous loop: pre-flight auth smoke, mechanical cycle-outcome ledger and fast-fail paging
tasks.summary: Delivered: the loop trigger now runs a bounded one-turn pre-flight smoke of the headless runtime before launching and, on failure, launches nothing, files an alert task and pages; the service manager records every launched cycle's outcome mechanically; the watchdog pages when three consecutive recorded cycles end within seconds. Root cause of the nine-day outage recorded: a stale headless CLI on the service path could not refresh its expired token while interactive use could. Tests 23/23 and 51/51; verified live with a real smoke, a simulated expired-token runtime, and a replay of the real outage.
tasks.next_action: Observe the 16:20 and 20:20 UTC trigger slots after the token expiry: a failed refresh must now page and file a task instead of silently launching dead cycles. Separate finding filed: mission write routes accept unauthenticated local callers.

tasks.title: Mission store: authenticate every write route (create, edit, tape, decision ruling) — no unauthenticated local caller
tasks.summary: Delivered: every mission-store write (create, edit, event-tape append, decision ruling) now requires a real credential; anonymous, wrong-token and identity-header-only callers are refused and nothing is written; observers are refused with an audit row; a sandboxed engineering agent may edit only work it currently holds, closing a reword-then-claim escalation; rulings are board-only; rows and audit name the authenticated actor. New tests 27/27 (26 failed before the fix), suite 339, real-money bolt 10/10, paper gate confirmed. An independent adversarial verification against the running service confirmed the refusals and that nothing was written; the observer refusal is proven in the harness only. Every existing writer already sent credentials, so nothing broke.
tasks.next_action: Filed for follow-up: the console's server-side proxy still grants operator authority to anonymous callers (high); the lease-sweep route has no auth (low); the loop's failure path marks a blocked mission with an invalid column (medium). Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item.

tasks.title: Console: require a verified operator session for every mission-store write made through the console, and name the human in the audit trail
tasks.summary: Delivered: every write made through the console to the mission store now requires a verified operator session — an HttpOnly signed cookie from a one-time operator sign-in, or a verified edge-login identity; anonymous, spoofed-identity, forged-cookie and forged-edge-token writes are refused at the console before the store is contacted, and a cross-site browser context is refused even with a session. Reads are unchanged. The audit trail now names the signed-in person instead of a generic operator. New tests 37 (all failed before the fix), console suite 304, real-money bolt 10/10, paper gate confirmed. An independent adversarial verification against the running console (private network and edge included) confirmed every refusal and the attribution; the positive edge-login path is proven in the harness only. Two of its low findings (sign-in lockout, key-set refresh flooding) were fixed in-cycle; the rest filed.
tasks.next_action: Filed for follow-up: a console rewrite forwards every method to the trading backend without a gate (high); reads through the console proxy still carry operator authority (low); session hardening — revocation on sign-out, stricter origin check (low). Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: a blocked cycle outcome must be recorded on the mission board (the store refused the marker the loop sent)
tasks.summary: Delivered: a blocked cycle outcome now lands on the mission board. The loop's finish step marks the held mission with the store's supported paused flag, keeps the reason comment, and hands the lease back, so the item shows as paused, is skipped by the work queue and the watchdog digest names it instead of paging. The test harness's fake store now enforces the real column contract and pagination (it previously accepted a value the real store rejects), and store-level tests pin the contract. Proven on a scratch copy of the real store (old path refused with an error and wedged; new path lands), then independently verified: holds with caveats. Two follow-ups fixed in-cycle (paged revision lookup, fixture label); negative-path hardening filed.
tasks.next_action: Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item — candidates: loop finish negative-path hardening (re-claim on a reaped lease, idempotent comment, reason on the row), console session hardening, reads through the console proxy carrying operator authority.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: a blocked cycle must still land on the board when its work lease has lapsed, must not duplicate its record on retry, and must show the reason
tasks.summary: Complete: the loop's blocked-outcome step now re-claims its work item once when the lease has lapsed and retries (it fails loudly with exact recovery steps only when someone else holds the item), records its outcome only after the state change lands and never twice, and puts the reason on the item so the board and the watchdog digest show why. Landed on master 2e9bfd0; independent verification on a copy of the live store: HOLDS; safety checks unchanged (paper only).

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the shared-checkout git guard must never fail closed when the home directory variable is missing, and the watchdog must page again for a build workspace that reappears at a path it already retired
tasks.summary: Complete: the shared-checkout git guard now hands through to real git when the home directory variable is missing (it previously aborted every governed command with a shell error) while still refusing destructive operations in the protected checkout; the loop watchdog now re-opens its own retired page, under the same identifier and with refreshed details, when a build workspace reappears at a path it had already retired, on every filing path, and never forces open a record it did not file. Both failures were reproduced on the previous code before fixing. Landed on master 500bea4; live watchdog run clean; installed guard proven live; independent verification holds with findings, the actionable ones fixed before merge and two pre-existing gaps tracked as new items; safety checks unchanged (paper only).

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the watchdog must re-open its own archived page for a build workspace that reappears, instead of failing to file a duplicate every run
tasks.summary: Complete: the mission store's list view now has an opt-in switch to include archived records (default unchanged), and the loop watchdog uses it to find its own archived pages and re-open them under the same identifier instead of failing to file a duplicate on every run; the watchdog still audits only live records, an archived rectify record counts as acknowledged for all three self-filed identifier families, and a watchdog running against a store that predates the switch degrades to a digest warning rather than a false unreachable page. Both failures were reproduced on the previous code first, including against a real scratch store. Landed on master 355effa; store service restarted on the merged code; live probes and a live watchdog run clean; independent verification holds with findings, the actionable ones fixed before merge; safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the store unit's inline environment value (tracked) and the 2026-09-10 watchdog-journal re-checks remain open.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the launch trigger must clear its own runtime-health alert page once the runtime is proven healthy again, and label a temporary usage-limit failure as temporary
tasks.summary: Complete: the loop's launch trigger now closes its own runtime-check and identity alert records on the first slot where the check passes again (only records it filed, never one another worker is actively holding, with a note explaining why), labels a temporary usage-limit failure as temporary with its reset time instead of asking for a re-login, treats alert records as never being work for a cycle, and re-checks a timed-out close before calling it a failure. Reproduced first in the trigger's test suite (nine new cases red on the previous code), then verified against the real record store: the stale record from earlier today closed itself on the first passing check. Independent verification held with findings; the actionable ones were fixed before merge and two lower-priority follow-ups were recorded. Landed on master 8b71afe; the timer picks up the merged script on its next slot with no restart; safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; follow-ups recorded for a lock-suite false positive when run inside an agent session and for alert-record wording that hides some records from sandboxed agents.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the research-recommendation bridge must stop re-filing already-delivered recommendations under new wording, keep the full recommendation on the record it files, and verify delivery against durable evidence
tasks.summary: Complete: the bridge that turns research notes into board records now keeps its de-duplication text on the record it files (using the fields the store actually keeps), reads the whole record list including archived rows, recognises a recommendation by the concrete artifacts it names so rewording no longer creates a new record (a recommendation adding a genuinely new artifact is still filed), skips past-tense reports to the board, and verifies delivered work against durable, fresh evidence rather than a liveness probe. Reproduced first in a new test suite (red on the previous code), then proven against the real record store: the merged script ran live and filed nothing for the six current restatements while verifying every delivered record. Six open duplicate records were closed with evidence; one follow-up was recorded for the research agent's own lane (it cannot see the delivered files from its sandbox). Independent verification held with findings; seven were fixed before merge. Landed on master f9fb8a9; no restart needed; safety checks unchanged (paper only).

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: console operator sign-in hardening — a sign-out must invalidate the session on the server, the browser-origin check must use a fixed allowlist rather than caller-set headers, sign-out itself must be same-origin, and a bad audit label must be rejected rather than silently replaced
tasks.summary: Complete: a console sign-out now invalidates the session on the server (a copied session value stops working at once, and a sign-out-everywhere option retires every earlier session without rotating any credential); the browser-origin check for writes uses an exact, explicit allowlist of the console's own addresses instead of headers a caller can set, so other services on the same host name are no longer acceptable origins; sign-in and sign-out refuse cross-site requests; an invalid audit label is rejected with a clear message rather than silently replaced. Test-first in the console unit suite (319 cases), proven on a scratch server, then landed on master 942803f, built and deployed with one restart, and re-proven live. Independent verification held with findings; a multi-process lost-write race, the port-less allowlist and eleven unlocked test properties were fixed before merge. Existing console sessions were invalidated by design (one re-sign-in). Safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the read-side operator-token injection through the console proxy remains a separate open item.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the console's read path must stop granting operator-level access to anonymous readers — the server-side operator credential is attached to a read only when the caller holds a verified console session
tasks.summary: Complete: the console's server-side proxy now attaches the operator credential to a read only when the caller holds a verified console session (sign-in cookie or edge login); an anonymous reader gets the mission store's own public read surface and the store's own refusal on the few privileged reads (council lock, agent soul/memory, agent queue, token accounting, paid-service control plane). The fleet view asks for council locks only when signed in, so anonymous viewers see the roster without a failed request on every refresh; the read-only acceptance suite now signs in when the credential is available and signs out afterwards. Test-first in the console unit suite (323 cases), proven on a scratch server with forged cookies, spoofed headers, signed-in, cross-site and revoked-session probes plus a headless-browser check of the fleet view, then landed on master 8e03da4, built and deployed with one restart, and re-proven live: an anonymous identity check through the console now reports no principal. Independent verification held with findings; an acceptance-session leak on overlapping runs, a file-mode window, a log-noise regression and a timer edge were fixed before merge; two pre-existing items were recorded separately (the acceptance specs are stale since the shell de-scoping; a store edit with a quoted precondition header errors). Safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the stale acceptance specs and the store precondition-header error are queued as their own items.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the console's read-only acceptance gate must reflect the de-scoped shell — expected stations and legacy redirects derive from the platform's plugin flags, and the retired desk routes are asserted as not-found when the plugin is off
tasks.summary: Complete: the console's read-only browser acceptance suite now derives its expected station strip, mast segments, legacy-redirect map and retired trading routes from the same configuration the shell uses, keyed on the platform's plugin flag, so it matches the de-scoped deck instead of the pre-de-scoping layout. Retired trading routes are asserted to render the not-found recovery card with the address untouched; the schedules negative asserts the current audited pause gate instead of self-skipping. Proven test-first: the unmodified suite failed 57 of 135 checks on the live console; the updated suite passes all 147 checks in both anonymous and signed-in modes, and a deliberate flag mismatch fails loudly with a one-line hint. Independent verification held with findings, all fixed before merge except one pre-existing build-flag caveat recorded as its own item. Landed on master b631c0c; test harness and runbook only, no runtime change, safety checks unchanged (paper only). While proving the merge the gate caught a real upstream fault: the console's proxy kept every live-status stream open forever, exhausting the mission store's file handles; mitigated with one console restart and taken up as the next item.
tasks.next_action: Fix the console proxy so live-status streams are passed through and closed when the viewer disconnects (second item of this cycle).

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the console's proxy must pass live-status streams through and close the upstream connection when the viewer disconnects — every page view was leaving a permanent connection open to the mission store until it ran out of file handles
tasks.summary: Complete: the console proxy now relays the mission store's live-status stream to the browser as a stream and tears the upstream request down when the viewer disconnects; every other response is proxied exactly as before and the access gate is unchanged. Root cause: the proxy buffered the never-ending stream in memory and never aborted it, so each page view leaked one upstream connection until the store ran out of file handles and answered server errors (seen during the first post-merge acceptance run). Proven test-first on a scratch build (frames flow, connections released even under thirty concurrent viewers and abrupt disconnects), covered by a new browser exit-gate test that fails on the old build, independently verified (held with findings, all addressed), landed on master b25fe81, built and deployed with one restart, and re-proven live: frames flow, connections track live viewers, both acceptance modes pass all 150 checks with zero store errors. Safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the build-flag caveat and the lock-release-at-cycle-end gap are queued as their own items.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the loop trigger must treat a launched-but-not-yet-locked cycle as running — its running-cycle check only looked for the lock file, so a second trigger run in the minutes before a cycle locks started a second concurrent cycle on the same lane (observed twice in four minutes on the trading lane)
tasks.summary: Complete: the loop trigger's running-cycle gate now asks the service manager whether any cycle unit of its own lane is already active before it looks at the lock file, and stands down while one exists — read-only, time-bounded, fail-closed on a probe error, lane-scoped, and stateless (a crashed cycle simply is not active). Root cause: the gate keyed only on the single-flight lock, which a launched cycle creates minutes later, so a second trigger run inside that window started a second concurrent cycle. Each launched cycle now writes its own output file (a stable link points at the latest) so duplicate or killed cycles stay attributable. Proven test-first (14 new cases, suite 68 to 82; the same cases fail 12 times against the old script), independently verified (held with findings, all addressed; the verifier reproduced the double launch on the old script and saw exactly one launch under concurrent triggers on the new), landed on master 3ad5e45 with no restart needed, and re-proven with the deployed script against this cycle's own live unit. Safety checks unchanged (paper only).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the watchdog blind spot for a long-running cycle that never locks and the dispatcher's keyword routing are queued as their own items.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the console's pass-through to the desk backend must be read-only — the path-level rewrite forwarded every HTTP method to the backend with no gate, so an anonymous caller who could reach the console could reach backend write routes and bypass the aggregator's mutation denylist (paper routes only; the real-money bolt and live gate were never reachable)
tasks.summary: Complete: the console's pass-through to the desk backend is now read-only — a dedicated handler forwards GET and HEAD and answers every other method 405 before any upstream contact, replacing the method-agnostic path rewrite (which is now guarded against reappearing in any form). Root cause: a framework-level rewrite forwards whatever method arrives, so the client-side read-only guarantee never constrained the server path and the aggregator's mutation denylist was not in the loop. Proven test-first (15 contract cases, suite 333 to 348; a request-level exit-gate spec fails 15 times against the old build and passes 21 of 21 on the new), independently verified (held with findings, all addressed: a recording upstream saw only reads across a 50-probe battery of method, smuggling and path tricks, and re-adding the rewrite was shown to bypass the handler), landed on master 7930c5e, built and restarted once, and re-proven live: every write 405 with zero bytes, reads byte-identical, the backend's own log shows zero writes and eleven reads from the proof run. Safety checks unchanged (paper only, real-money bolt tests pass before and after). Two sibling pass-throughs were audited and queued as their own items (the automation assistant's path forwards every method with no caller gate; the fleet path points at a retired upstream).
tasks.next_action: Next loop cycle picks the next open item; the automation-assistant pass-through gate and the retired fleet path are queued as their own items.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the console's pass-through to the automation assistant must gate writes — the path-level rewrite forwarded every HTTP method with no caller gate, so an anonymous caller who could reach the console could invoke the assistant's decision and tuning routes (paper only; the real-money bolt and live gate were never reachable)
tasks.summary: Complete: the console's pass-through to the automation assistant is now gated — a dedicated handler forwards reads without credentials, allows exactly the three deck actions (chat, conductor dispatch, policy save) only for a verified operator session in a same-origin context, refuses every other write path (decision, tuning, propose, mission-event) even when signed in, and answers every other method 405, all before any upstream contact — replacing the method-agnostic rewrite (now guarded against reappearing by text and by source-pattern evaluation). Root cause: a framework-level rewrite forwards whatever method arrives and the assistant has no caller authentication of its own. Proven test-first (31 contract cases, suite 348 to 379; a request-level exit-gate spec runs behind a fail-safe canary that aborts on an ungated build), independently verified (held with findings, all addressed: a recording upstream saw only the allowed writes and never a credential header across a 75-probe path/protocol battery; re-adding the rewrite was shown to bypass the handler; the deck's own actions were driven in a headless browser), landed on master 0ee203d, built and restarted once, and re-proven live: every anonymous write refused with zero upstream lines, reads byte-identical, full deck exit gate 222 of 222 signed-in. Disclosed: the cycle's first negative proof ran the spec against the old build and so exercised the exposure itself (inert outcomes; the spec is now fail-safe). Safety checks unchanged (paper only, real-money bolt tests pass before and after).

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the single-flight lock must be released mechanically when a cycle's process exits — a cycle that spent its last turn on the handover text left the lock held, so the next scheduled slot skipped and the following cycle only started an hour later via stale-owner recovery
tasks.summary: In progress: the loop's single-flight lock stayed held after a cycle's process had already exited (the cycle ended its final turn before the explicit release), so the scheduler skipped a slot and recovery waited on the stale-owner timeout. Fix: the service manager's post-exit hook releases the lock when it can prove the lock belongs to the run that just ended (same run identity, owning process gone), with durable evidence; test-first, then independent verification.
